newsitem.title: CANADA: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

CANADA, July 28 - Vancouver, BC - Roberts Bank - Coal terminal berth number 2 is out of service until 29/7 for servicing. Berth number 1 is operating normally, The U.S. and Western Canada salmon dispute is not affecting commercial shipping at any west coast Canadian port. Both sides have indicated that they will renegotiate. Approx. 10 days waiting for grain vessels for Japan, and 3-4 days for other grades.

HONDURAS, July 28 - Puerto Cortes - Six vessels berthed of which 3 discharging/loading containers/generals, 1 discharging explosives, 1 discharging fertiliser, 1 loading lumber. 2 Vessels anchored of which 1 to discharge/load containers/generals, 1 to load zinc concentrates. 16 Due of which 1 passenger, 8 to discharge/load containers/generals, 6 to discharge/load containers/bananas, 1 to discharge steel products. Vessels berthed, 4 discharging/loading containers, 1 discharging wheat, 1 discharging urea, 1 passenger vessel discharging vehicles. Vessels awaiting berth, 5 to discharge/load containers, 2 to discharge wheat, 1 discharging iron. Vessels due, 5 to discharge bananas, 7 to load/discharger containers, 1 to discharge wheat. Port congested. Rainy season.

PANAMA, July 28 - Cristobal, Balboa - Working normally. Panama Canal - Waterway operating normally, and transit reservation system at condition 1. 41 Vessels due, 47 in queue, 18 booked, 40 scheduled.

UNITED STATES, July 28 - Hampton Roads, Va - Six general cargo/container vessels operating. 3 Bulkers loading coal, 3 anchored waiting to load. 1 Bulker discharging cement. 1 Vessel in pier under repair.

EAST COAST - Baltimore MD - No congestion at Dundalk terminal anticipated this week. Clear c/d canal/Baltimore harbour low ceiling. Elevators and coal operations working well with no delays. Average waiting time Consol Coal 3 days. Liquid bulk facilities - Operating normal, no berthing congestion. Anchorage available at Baltimore and Annapolis. Charleston, SC - No vessels scheduled at shipyard river coal terminal or grain elevator. No delays expected at tanker terminals. All terminals up and running. Columbus Street, north Charleston and Wando terminal - Will be light. One crane at Columbus Street terminal will be down the first week of August for about 4 days for repairs. Miami - No major delays are expected for berthing at either port of Miami or Port Everglades. No congestion expected. Passenger terminals are available from Tuesday to Thursday and from Friday 0600 hrs. to Monday 1900 hrs. New York, NY - No congestion in New York anchorages. No congestion in tanker terminals and no congestion in sugar t

Norfolk, VA - Norfolk Southern Coal pier - Expecting 9 vessels during this week. Presently, 4 vessels are anchored waiting to load. Dominion terminal - Expecting 11 vessels. Pier IX terminal - Expecting 5 vessels during the next week. Norfolk Southern Coal pier 6 has completed its maintenance and both loaders are now operating. Container and general cargo terminals are working normally with no delays. Oil and bulk terminals are working normally. Construction is near completion on the work over the Norfolk international terminal, pier 3, where frozen chicken exports are expected to begin during early autumn. Philadelphia, PA - There is no port congestion in the ports of Philadelphia, Camden, Wilmington. No activity as far as dredging/repairs/navigational problems.

GULF COAST - Houston, TX - No congestion at the port of Houston city docks, Houston public grain elevator and Cargill grain elevator. However, congestion exists at Farmland grain elevator, Galveston. Approx. 2-3 days waiting at some oil/chemical terminals. New Orleans, LA - It is normal for periods of rain to occur during summer season and these cause delays in cargo operation especially grain loading. Grain shipments normal for this season. River stage at 4.1 feet, expected to drop to 3.5 ft. by 31 July. High river will cause delays in ship movement and vessel transit times. Bar pilots advise that the draft for the Mississippi River gulf outlet will be 36 ft. Present max. permissible draft at S.W. Pass is 46 ft. Fresh water for vessels under 100,000 dwt, 45 ft. Fresh water for vessels over 100,000 dwt. Based on these drafts, all vessels are to maintain sufficient airdraft for transit under bridges in Mississippi River. Some elevators are not working weekends due to slower than usual grain shipments.

WEST COAST - Columbia River - Grain vessel activity appears to be increasing. There are 4 vessels loading and 4 vessels waiting at anchorage. The port of Kalama north terminal will be ready to accept its first vessel around the first week of September. This terminal will be operated by BHP Australia and will process inbound steel coils. Coos Bay - Vessel traffic busy this past week. Two woodchip carriers loading, 2 loading lumber, 1 log vessel loading at Dolphin terminal, and one nickel vessel discharging at Glenbrook terminal. This coming week vessel traffic is expected to decrease. Delays to vessel traffic due to fog, no berthing congestion. Channel opening project under way in upper shipping channel, and expected to be completed in the autumn. Honolulu and Barbers Point - the ILWU negotiations continue between young brothers and the company longshoremen. No strike has been announced and interisland barge service continues as normal. The current small craft advisories are expected to continue for the co

Long Beach and Los Angeles - Pilots strike - The state superior court has granted a temporary restraining order, preventing L.A. pilots from picketing terminals until July 30 at which time the court will re-evaluate status of city/pilot contract negotiations. A federal court has decided not to take this issue under consideration until after superior court has ruled. To date pilots are officially still on strike. However, vessels are moving into/out of the port of Los Angeles with 3 management pilots causing minimal delays. The ILWU longshoremen are again working the vessels in port of Los Angeles. The port of Long Beach is not affected by the situation at the port of Los Angeles. Port of Long Beach has advised they will not accept any vessel diversions to Long Beach from Los Angeles for discharge due to possibility of the strike situation following such vessels to Long Beach.
